summary: The primary body-width estimand is clearly defined as the median representative-plane apparent body width among technically valid nuclei, summarized once per biological specimen. Commit-bound outputs correctly suppress inference for the one-specimen-per-group candidate, preserve missing-width diagnostics in technical QC, separate count and density denominators, and pass cross-format numeric validation. Acceptance is blocked because the report generator still infers the reference group from hard-coded control/WT/w1118 genotype tokens when explicit group direction is omitted, contrary to the required reporting check.

findings.title: Primary report can infer group direction from hard-coded genotype labels
findings.impact: A report generated without explicit group arguments silently interprets labels such as WT, w1118, wild, or control as the reference group. This embeds genotype semantics in reporting, can reverse signed effects for differently named studies, and violates the explicit requirement to reject hard-coded genotype labels in primary biological reports.

findings.recommendation: Require explicit reference/comparison arguments or validated study-role metadata for every primary report. Remove label-token inference from the v5.7.1 reporting path, fail closed when direction is absent, add adversarial neutral-label tests, and generate a superseding commit-bound report receipt.

limitations: No full image stack was run, as requested.

Cross-format agreement was assessed from the commit-bound validation receipt and numeric contract rather than regenerating the PDF or workbook.
Other reviewers' outputs were not read.
